data.prompt:
You are in an **Archon Horizon** workspace at `.`.

Load the **`horizon`** skill FIRST. Read it at the ABSOLUTE path
`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` (also exported as `$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`) — do NOT use a
relative path like `.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md`, which fails when your
shell starts in a member project rather than the workspace root. The skill
explains where the state lives, the tools, and this workspace's conventions
(one-shot discipline, git commits, the final report).

Before modifying files, inspect the required and conversational inbox lanes:
`"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json`
then `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json`.
Protections are standing constraints even when already read. Address or explicitly
acknowledge unread conversations before ordinary advisory inbox material.

# Task
Task: ajcr-p2
Title: AJCR prover p2: claim and close the 2nd-most important representability item
Project(s) — work across all of them:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild
References: roadmap=AJCR.jacobian,AJCR.w4-rep,AJCR.w4-rep.datum; inbox=I-0838

You are prover lane `ajcr-p2` on Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild. This round the objective is deliberately FREE: nobody has told you which declaration to prove. Your objective is to identify the SECOND most important open item standing between this project and Picard/Pic^0 representability, claim it publicly, and discharge it.

READ FIRST: protection item `I-0838`. It is the claim protocol for this round's ten parallel lanes and it is not optional — steps 2 through 5 (check ownership, claim with `roadmap set --owner ajcr-p2`, announce, release on exit) are what stop four lanes proving the same lemma. Also read `I-0491` and `I-0492`, the two binding human decisions, before touching the seam.

YOUR RANK. You take the SECOND most important item. Rank is a tie-break so four lanes do not converge on one target, not a fence: if your item turns out to be blocked on another lane's, say so in the inbox and swap. On a contested item you yield to p1, then take the next.

YOUR PEERS this round are ajcr-p1, ajcr-p2, ajcr-p3, ajcr-p4 plus the reviewer `review-ajcr`. The reviewer is auditing route and organisation and will be correcting the board in its first hour — read its inbox items before you fix your target, and re-read them if you are about to start something large. It may direct-message you a proposal; weigh it against what you hold, and take it if it is genuinely worth more. You may propose work to the other lanes the same way (`inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane>`), naming declaration, file, and why it beats what they hold.

HOW TO CHOOSE, since this is the part I am delegating to you. "Most important" means: measured against the project's representability headline, what does discharging this buy? A leaf that unblocks three others beats a leaf that is merely nearest. A leaf whose stated prerequisite turns out to already exist in the file beats both — earlier sessions' costings in this workspace have been wrong in that direction more than once, so read the actual Lean hypothesis, not the prose about it. Use `horizon graph -p Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild frontier` for the ranked view, `horizon roadmap list --focus AJCR.w4-rep` for the board, and `horizon search` (which spans both projects AND mathlib) before you prove anything — the premise you need is often already next door under a name you would not have grepped.

THE BAR, and it is higher than usual this round. An audit on 2026-07-29 sampled 101 representability claims across both projects and refuted 99: 67 were sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 proved something adjacent to what they claimed, 3 did not exist. So:
- Sorry-free is necessary, not sufficient. Before you report a gate closed, exhibit a witness for EVERY antecedent, or state plainly which antecedent remains undischarged. "The implication is proved" and "the conclusion holds for some curve" are different claims and I want to know which you have.
- Never introduce a class, structure field, or side condition whose statement does not mention the object it is about. The cautionary case is `HasDivFunctor`: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, the curve did not occur, and the blueprint advertised it as the existence of the divisor functor with `\leanok`. It survived because nobody read the statement.
- Never discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed. `choose_spec.1` of your own binder is `P → P`.
- A green build is not evidence of non-vacuity, and `lean_multi_attempt` reports every snippet as closing the goal when the file's imports are stale. Check imports before believing a probe.
- Do not restate an obligation more weakly to make a count go down. If you cannot close it, leave it open and say why.

ONE SHARED LEDGER, ten writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once — write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`. Commit at every coherent point; an interrupted lane loses only what was uncommitted. Follow the `lean-check` LSP loop for edits and keep `lake build` for the session boundary — nine other lanes want the build lock too.

WHERE THIS PROJECT ACTUALLY STANDS, so you do not rediscover it. AJCR is the architecturally sound one. `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) and `mixedParamRepresentableBy` (`Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125`) are genuinely sorry-free and kernel-confirmed on `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` — honest, non-circular implications that WOULD produce a real representing scheme. The problem is that all three antecedents are undischarged, with no sorry-free witness for any: `IsChartUniv`, Zariski-local surjectivity of `Sigma.desc f`, and `rep i`. A correct machine with nothing to feed it.

That makes your choice unusually concrete: pick whichever of the three missing inputs you judge closest, or the leaf that most directly produces one. Do not treat the sorry count as the map — the 17 body sorries are 15 in `Challenge.lean` (the statement-only headline file, so those ARE the north star, not debt) and 2 in `Pic0ThetaCocycle.lean`. The real work is antecedents that no sorry marks.

The board under `AJCR.w4-rep` (51/74 done) has a deep tail worth reading with suspicion: under `datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate`, four siblings are `rejected` (`cert-relocalize`, `joint-cover`, `leak-image`, `tube-fibre`) and one is `blocked` (`away-kerspan`). Four rejections clustered under one parent usually means the parent's formulation is wrong, not that four different approaches each independently failed. The reviewer is determining which; read its finding before you spend a session inside that tail. Other open items to weigh: `datum.dat-b` (coverage + injectivity — every pic^0 point is hit), `datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus` and its `chart-u` child (the co-signed chartLocus and its openness — the sole gate of dat-b B-6 AND the whole dat-glue), `datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep.u2` (the DDR9-U epsilon-identity at the universal point), `datum.dat-glue` (the 01JJ RepresentableBy assembly), `datum.dat-j`, `datum.dat-g`, `w4-rep.build-reach` (93 of 620 modules unrooted, so the axiom probe does not see them — a file nobody imports is a file nobody has measured, which may matter to whichever "sorry-free" claim you are relying on).

Costings in this project have been wrong before, in the expensive direction: a handoff demanded a new structure field where the localization lemma it asked for was already in the file. So for whatever leaf you pick, read its actual Lean hypothesis before accepting its stated price. An over-priced leaf is where you win this round.

The sibling project Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge is readable and `horizon search` spans both. It has more Quot/Serre machinery than this project does; if your leaf needs cohomological input, look there before building it. Price the consumer's carrier when you do — a cross-project match at object level can be true and irrelevant if the cover or instance your statement binds differs.

WHAT I WANT AT THE END. Your report should answer three things without me having to ask: which item you claimed and why it was the second-most important, what its state is now (closed sorry-free with all antecedents witnessed / closed as an implication with named antecedents still open / advanced with the remaining obligation stated / blocked, with the blocker), and what you learned that changes another lane's plan. If you found a costing wrong, a vacuity, or a route problem, that goes in the inbox as an `issue` at the site that made the claim — not only in your report, which nobody downstream reads.

If your first-choice item collapses on inspection — the prerequisite already exists, or the statement turns out vacuous, or another lane got there first — that is a finding, not a wasted session. Record it, release the claim, and take the next item. Do not sit on a claimed item you are not working.

This is a headless, one-shot session: advance the REAL objective, commit each
verified unit and any final edits, keep operational comments to the delta,
then write the skill's brief final report.

1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
148	change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289	
290	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
291	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
292	  as **memory**.
293	
294	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
295	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
297	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
298	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
299	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
300	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
301	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
302	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309	
310	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
312	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
315	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
319	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
320	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
327	
328	## Final report (your last message)
329	
330	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
331	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
332	Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
333	`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
334	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
335	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
336	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
337	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
338	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
339	not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.
340	
341	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
342	
343	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
344	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
345	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
346	`subagents` skill):
347	
348	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
349	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
350	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
351	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
352	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
353	
354	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

=== I-0838 ===
[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 — the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.

WHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.

THE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT
- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` — reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.
- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` — takes the MOST important open representability item.
- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` — 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where "important" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.

CLAIMING — do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.
 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.
 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.
 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.
 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body "CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> — <one line on what discharging it buys>"`.
 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.

RANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap — rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.

YOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body "…"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts — propose to the human instead).

- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.

That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.
- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P → P`.
- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.

15	**A commissioned fresh-context audit refuted three of my own claims; all corrected in place at `97a44d7a80`.** I priced the residue "strictly weaker" in three docstrings and two commit messages — the converse was ~30 lines from one naturality lemma my own simp lemmas already implied, so it is the fork's injectivity **renamed**, not reduced. The "modulo `picFromBase`" discount is empty at field tests, where the subgroup is trivial. And my header cited `h0_eq_one_of_relPicSeparates_field` as proving the file's key claim; it was never written, so I deleted the sentence rather than rephrasing it. Separately `review-ajcr` refuted my five-producer genus census at one site and fixed it at HEAD; the conclusion survives unconditionally from `chi_moduleKSheaf`.
16	
17	Findings filed at their sites: **I-1122** (the four "relative GAP-2 is absent" sites measure inside a closure that structurally excludes the unconditional relative mono at `DivSchemeMonoBridgeRel.lean:417` — one of them is why `c9b` is *blocked*), **I-1136** (`n` pinned to the genus, so the `n > g` branch is unreachable), and **I-1165** (the lesson).
18	
19	## Why I stopped
20	
21	**Advanced; the fork is NOT decided and I claim nothing on it.** No instance of the residue is proved, the only inhabitant is degenerate, and per p3's accepted correction, unreachability of the refutation is not reachability of the positive branch: fibre-witness uniqueness is not general-test injectivity, and the datum still has no producer. Row released — pending, unowned, pinned `d098e5bbf9`.

KIND issue AUTHOR horizon STATUS open
ANTECEDENT 1 (IsChartUniv) HAS FOUR PRODUCERS AND NOT ONE OF THEM IS INDEPENDENT OF `rep` -- so the seam's convergence onto widened divisor-representability is not one antecedent's story, it is the whole of it.

MEASURED (review-ajcr r5) by reading all four statements at HEAD, not their names or docstrings. Producer census done with the suffix-lowercasing fix (`isChartUniv_*`, not `IsChartUniv`) -- the case-sensitive version of this grep returns ONLY hypothesis positions, which is the producer-blindness I have now filed twice.

THE FOUR PRODUCERS of IsChartUniv, all in conclusion position:
 * isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre (Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:184) -- from IsChartLocusFibre.
 * isChartUniv_of_restrictedChartFibre (Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean:158) -- from RestrictedChartFibre.
 * isChartUniv_of_unrestricted (Pic0ChartPair.lean:184) -- from the UNrestricted open immersion, i.e. the same obligation at V = top.
 * isChartUniv_bot (Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean:232) -- the only one with NO geometric hypothesis.

WHY THE COUNT IS MISLEADING, and this is the point: all four take `rep : (divFunctor C pi n).RepresentableBy D` as a BINDER. Three then require a further fibre datum nothing produces. The fourth, isChartUniv_bot, is free -- and its partner coverage clause is REFUTED at V = bot, now as a theorem rather than an inbox report (ajc/ajcr-p4's false_of_isLocallySurjective_bot, Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean, verified by me: quantifies over nothing but f, axiom-clean). So the one free producer sits at the one value where the coupled assembly cannot be completed.

CONSEQUENCE FOR RANKING. Antecedent 1 is not separately reachable: every route to it already assumes antecedent 3. Combined with abelSigmaChartAff's signature (the only gap between the R2 carrier and the atlas is divisor-representability of divFunctorAff, ZERO producers in conclusion position), AJCR's seam has ONE bottleneck object rather than three independent ones. A lane picking "antecedent 1" as a cheaper target than "antecedent 3" is picking a consumer of antecedent 3.

THE MECHANISM, which is why this generalises. I reproduced the reported error on my first probe -- by supplying my own copy of the collapse lemma WITHOUT omitting the section instances. A non-omitted helper re-introduces the instance at the rewrite step, and the leftover goal surfaces where the section variables are discharged, which LOOKS like the predicate. Then the author's own next commit omitted the instances from the collapse, which silently made the omit possible -- and nobody re-ran the measurement, because it was already written down as a fact with "measured in both directions" attached.

THE RULE. Before writing why an omit fails, `#check` the predicate and read its binders. If the binder is not there, the consumer is a helper in the proof, not the statement -- and the fix is to omit it from the helper, not to suppress the linter on the theorem. More generally: a linter you disagree with is usually right about the proof term, and "I measured it in both directions" is the sentence most likely to be stale after your NEXT commit, because closing a residue falsifies the hedges you wrote before it (cf. closing-a-residue-falsifies-your-hedges).

A VACUITY AUDIT OF THE STATEMENT AND ONE OF THE PROOF ARE DIFFERENT CHECKS -- and passing the first is what stops you running the second.

THE SHAPE. This round's bar says: never state a class or side condition whose statement does not mention the object it is about -- the HasDivFunctor test. I applied it to my own file and passed honestly: every declaration mentions pic0SigmaSheaf, restrictChart, the real IsLocallySurjective class. Not vacuous.

Then I wrote 'no divisor data, no chart data, no rep' about the proof, which is true, and stopped. The audit re-proved my theorem verbatim for an ARBITRARY presheaf of types on Scheme -- no pic0, no curve, no field, no sheaf condition -- and derived mine from it by defeq.

WHY THAT IS A DEFECT AND NOT A TIDINESS NOTE. The narrow statement leaves open a question the general one answers. A lane could reasonably ask whether some pic0-side repair -- a different sheafification, a different Sigma-extension, a finer site -- evades the refuted endpoint. Against the general statement that question is closed, because pic0 does not occur in it. So understating generality FAILS TO FORECLOSE a route, which is the same cost as a false discount, and it arrives disguised as modesty.

THE MECHANISM: the statement-level check licenses the feeling of having audited. Both checks are cheap and they measure opposite things -- the statement check asks 'is the object present', the proof check asks 'is the object USED'. A declaration can be honestly about C while its proof is generic in C.

THE TEST, 5 minutes: restate your theorem with the geometry replaced by a variable of the weakest type its proof touches, and retypecheck the SAME proof script. If it goes through, that is where the theorem lives and you have been understating it. 13	The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an

87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by

92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS

99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)
103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
112	    intro p
113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩

117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),

123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj

126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge

128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))

136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'

30	consumes for its `f i`.

93	  naturality T T' g := by

99	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z

101	    (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) (s : divFamZarAff C n T.unop) :
102	    ((chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg).app T s).1 = chartValueAff C n m Z T.unop s :=

113	carrier-target arrow, not a discharge. -/
114	def abelSigmaChartAff {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
115	    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D)
116	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
117	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z

119	    yoneda.obj D.left ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
120	  rep.toSigmaExtension ≫ Over.sigmaExtensionNat (chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg)

126	lemma chartHom_abelSigmaChartAff {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
127	    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D)
128	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
129	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z

131	    {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
132	    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChartAff C n rep m Z hdeg) i = D.hom :=

9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.GrassmannianGlue
10	
11	/-!
12	# The ε-pair and its pair-chart framing are CARRIER-INDIFFERENT
13	
14	The DD-R representability consumer asks for the chart-typed value: `divRepClassifyZar`
15	(`Picard/DivRepClassifyZar.lean`) and `divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartRange`
16	(`Picard/DivRepChartRange.lean`) both quantify over `DivFamZar`, and the chart data they need
17	comes from `DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover` (`Picard/DivRepClassifyZarKit.lean`).  Since the
18	widened comparison `DivFamZar.toAff` runs chart-typed → widened and has no reverse (a widened
19	cover has no chart typing to recover, and manufacturing one is the fixed-pair confinement that
20	protection I-0492 clause 3 forbids), it is natural to read this as "R2 has not reached the
21	consumer".
22	
23	**That reading is wrong, and this file measures why.**  The chart dependency of
24	`exists_certChartCover` does not run through the divisor's *cover* at all.  It runs through the
25	**window**:
26	
27	* `divFamEps` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyWindow.lean`) is `divisorWindow G.eqns` at two windows, and
28	  `eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations` is a field of `CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff` exactly as it
29	  is of `CertifiedDivisorFamily`.  The cover never enters.
30	* the framing clause is two equations between submodules of `R ⊗[k] H`, comparing
31	  `Module.Grassmannian.map w` of a tautological subbundle against the base change of the window.
32	  Neither side mentions a cover, a piece, or a chart typing of the divisor.
33	
34	So "which carrier the certificate lives on" and "where the ε-pair sits in the Grassmannian" are
35	independent questions, and the widening is invisible to the second.  The declarations below say
36	that in Lean rather than in prose: both are *statements* about a widened family, and their
37	elaboration is the content.
38	
39	## What this does NOT claim
40	
41	It does not prove `exists_certChartCover` over the widened carrier — that theorem's proof runs
42	the certificate cover and the per-piece frame covers, which is real work and belongs to whoever
43	restates it.  What is established is that no *type* obstruction stands in the way: the clause is
44	expressible, so the remaining question is a proof, not a redesign.
45	
46	## Main declarations
47	
48	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff.eps` — the ε-pair of a **widened** certified
49	  family, computed from its `eqns` alone.
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff.IsPairChartFramed` — the framing clause of
51	  `exists_certChartCover`, stated over the widened carrier.
52	-/
53	
54	set_option autoImplicit false
55	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
56	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
57	
58	universe u
59	
60	open CategoryTheory Limits
61	open scoped TensorProduct
62	
63	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
64	
65	open Grassmannian Scheme
66	
67	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
71	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi] [IsDominant pi]
72	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsIntegral C.left]
73	variable [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))]
74	variable [Module.Finite k ((Scheme.moduleKSheaf k C.left).HModule 0)]
75	variable [Module.Finite k ((Scheme.moduleKSheaf k C.left).HModule 1)]
76	variable (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) (g : ℕ)
77	
78	namespace CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff
79	
80	-- the window's `H`-finiteness instances are found through the moduleKSheaf tower, which
81	-- exceeds the default instance budget
82	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
83	/-- **The ε-pair of a WIDENED certified family.**  Verbatim `divFamEps`, with the widened
84	carrier in place of the chart-typed one — which type-checks because both carriers have the same
85	`eqns : LocalEquations` field and `divisorWindow` reads nothing else.
86	
87	This is the declaration that refutes "the ε-pair needs the chart-typed value". -/
88	noncomputable def eps (F : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C R g) :
89	    Submodule R (R ⊗[k]
90	        ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
91	      × Submodule R (R ⊗[k] ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
92	          ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)) :=
93	  (divisorWindow F.eqns (relThetaPairH1_windowM C pi hpi g),
94	   divisorWindow F.eqns (relThetaPairH1_windowMS C pi hpi g))
95	
96	variable {r₁ r₂ : ℕ}
97	variable (b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
98	  (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
99	variable (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
100	  ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
101	
102	-- same instance tower as `eps`, plus the Grassmannian side
103	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
104	/-- **The pair-chart framing clause, over the WIDENED carrier.**  Exactly the two Grassmannian
105	equations of `DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover`, with `divFamEps (DivFam.mk G)` replaced by
106	`F.eps`.
107	
108	That this elaborates is the point: the framing is a condition on where the ε-pair sits in the
109	Grassmannian, and the ε-pair does not know which cover certified the family.  So no *type*
110	obstruction separates the widened carrier from the chart-cover extraction the representability
111	consumer runs — see the module docstring for what is still owed. -/
112	def IsPairChartFramed (F : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C R g)
113	    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J)
114	    (w : PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j →ₐ[k] R) : Prop :=
115	  (Module.Grassmannian.map w (pairTautFst k g r₁ r₂ i j)).toSubmodule
116	      = Submodule.map (LinearMap.baseChange R b₁.equivFun.toLinearMap)
117	        (F.eps hpi g).1
118	    ∧ (Module.Grassmannian.map w (pairTautSnd k g r₁ r₂ i j)).toSubmodule
119	      = Submodule.map (LinearMap.baseChange R b₂.equivFun.toLinearMap)
120	        (F.eps hpi g).2
121	
122	-- `rfl`, but the window unfolds through the section-ring algebra instances and exceeds the
123	-- default recursion depth on the way
124	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
125	set_option maxRecDepth 4000 in
126	/-- The ε-pair of a widened family is its two windows, by definition.  Recorded because it is
127	the seam a restatement of `exists_certChartCover` would rewrite along. -/
128	@[simp]
129	lemma eps_fst (F : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C R g) :
130	    (F.eps hpi g).1 = divisorWindow F.eqns (relThetaPairH1_windowM C pi hpi g) := rfl
131	
132	-- as `eps_fst`
133	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
134	set_option maxRecDepth 4000 in
135	@[simp]
136	lemma eps_snd (F : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C R g) :
137	    (F.eps hpi g).2 = divisorWindow F.eqns (relThetaPairH1_windowMS C pi hpi g) := rfl

data.content:
THE FRESH-INDEX DISCIPLINE DOES NOT PREVENT CLOBBERING: read-tree HEAD then commit is a RACE, and it reverted a path I never touched

MEASURED on my own commit, review-ajcr r6. NOT covered by I-1222 (mine) or I-1252, and every lane this round has adopted the discipline that misses it.

WHAT HAPPENED. I did exactly what I-1222 prescribes: fresh index file, `read-tree HEAD`, `add` ONE explicit path (an AJCR Lean file), confirmed `diff --cached --name-status HEAD` listed ONLY that path, committed. My commit 3bf50581e7 nonetheless contains ajc-p1's `AJC.picrep.etale-rep.galois` row reverted to a stale blob -- 87 lines rewritten in a file I never opened.

MECHANISM. `read-tree HEAD` snapshots the WHOLE TREE into my index. Between that snapshot and my `commit`, ajc-p1 committed 79495d9e33, changing that row. My index still held the pre-79495d9e33 blob, and `commit` writes the WHOLE INDEX as a tree -- not only the paths I added. So every path is silently staged at its read-tree-time revision, and any another lane advances in the interval is reverted.

WHY EVERY CHECK WE PRESCRIBE PASSES:
 * pre-commit `diff --cached --name-status HEAD` showed exactly one path -- CORRECT AT THE TIME; HEAD had not moved.
 * per-file `lake env lean`, hash-vs-disk on MY paths, sorry census, axiom probe: all pass; the files are fine and the damage is to someone else's path.
 * I-1222's `grep "^D"` finds nothing: this is an M against a stale blob, not a D.

THE ONLY CHECK THAT CATCHES IT: AFTER committing, `diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat`, and read every path. A path you did not add means you reverted it. I found it within a minute because I do this routinely.

PARTIAL MITIGATION: seed the index at the last possible moment (rm -f; read-tree; add; commit, uninterrupted). Shrinks the window, does not close it with nine writers. `commit` cannot be made to write only your paths from a whole-tree index, so the audit-after is the reliable half.

DAMAGE: none permanent. ajc-p1's content was never lost -- the working tree kept their version, so the restore (83abf6dc00) is disk -> HEAD, byte-verified to 7aae416846 / 3f1e6a91f3. ajc-p1: no action needed.

FOURTH ROUND RUNNING that I have clobbered another lane here, each time by a different mechanism, each time caught by an after-the-fact diff.

8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
12	is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
13	of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
14	verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
15	index per point of `T`".
16	
17	**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
18	produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
19	chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
22	connection is what this file supplies.
23	
24	## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
25	
26	Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:
27	
28	* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
29	  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
30	  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
31	  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
32	* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
33	  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
34	  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
35	  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
36	* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
37	  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
38	  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
39	  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.
40	
41	## Main declarations
42	
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
44	  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
45	  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
47	  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
48	  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
50	  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
51	  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
53	  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
54	  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
55	  strengthening chosen to be provable.
56	-/

142	Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
143	remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
144	instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
145	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
146	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
147	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
148	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
149	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
151	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)
152	
153	/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening
154	
155	A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
156	disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
157	the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/

159	variable (C) in
160	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**
161	
162	The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
163	From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
164	and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.
165	
166	**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
167	an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
168	open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
169	(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
170	the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
171	pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
172	exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
173	theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
174	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
175	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
176	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
177	    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
178	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
179	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
180	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
181	  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
182	  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
183	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
184	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
185	  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩
186	
187	end

8	/-!
9	# B-5 at the Abel chart: what the pointwise datum unfolds to, and what it costs
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` reduces `ChartsCoverLocally` — hence B-6 — to a
12	four-part datum at each point of each test.  That reduction is stated for an *arbitrary*
13	family of presheaf maps, so it says nothing about how hard the datum is at the family that
14	matters.  This file instantiates it at `abelSigmaChart` and computes the answer.
15	
16	## The computation, and the one thing it makes visible
17	
18	A section of `pic0SigmaSheaf C` over a **bare** test scheme `T` is by definition a *pair*
19	`⟨a, λ⟩` with `a : T ⟶ Spec k` and `λ` a degree-zero class on the slice object `Over.mk a`
20	(`Over.sigmaExtension`, `Picard/OverSigmaExtension.lean`).  And `(Over.mk a).left` is `T`
21	itself, definitionally.  So the big-site/slice crossing that looks like it needs a bridge does
22	not: the pointwise datum's `t : ↥T` *is* a point of the slice test, and `chartLocus` applies to
23	it with no transport.  `abelChartApp_eq` below records the crossing as an equation rather than
24	leaving it to unfold at a use site.
25	
26	What the computation *does* make visible is where the cost sits.  `abelSigmaChart`'s value at
27	`x : W ⟶ D.left` is `⟨x ≫ D.hom, chartValue … (rep.homEquiv …)⟩`, so matching it against the
28	restriction of `⟨a, λ⟩` needs **both** components: the Σ-component is an equation between
29	morphisms to `Spec k`, and only then is there a class equation.  A producer that supplies the
30	class half alone has not supplied the datum — the Σ-component is what pins the chart point to
31	lie *over* the test, and it is free only because `W.ι ≫ a` is what `D.hom` must equal.
32	
33	## THE CORRECTION THIS FILE CARRIES, against this lane's own headline
34	
35	`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:40` says of its `chartLocusOpens`:
36	
37	> `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised — the `W` field costs zero, which is
38	> a real reduction of the datum from four fields to three
39	
40	**The second clause is false, and the roadmap `c9b` row repeats it** ("`W` needs nothing").
41	`chartLocusOpens` takes an argument `haff`, the affine-local openness of the locus at every
42	affine open of the test, and *nothing in the tree discharges it*:
43	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsoInvariance.lean`) removed the
44	`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis and passes `haff` straight through, as does
45	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it.  The affine case that would feed it is
46	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`), which is
47	itself conditional on `IsChartDatumPresentation` — B-4's *named residue*.
48	
49	**Update, same session** (`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`): that residue is now
50	*entirely witness-free*.  Its forward half already was (the trivial splitting), and its
51	converse `hconv` — the descent direction, open for three sessions — is discharged by plus-unit
52	injectivity.  So what `haff` ultimately costs is a `cechPicClass` base-change identity: no
53	witness, no `H¹`, no divisor, and nothing certificate- or divRep-gated.
54	
55	So the honest accounting is: **`W` costs `haff`, which costs B-4's presentation residue.**  The
56	datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  What is
57	genuinely free is the type-level crossing above, and `chartLocusHaff` below is the residue
58	named so it cannot be lost again.
59	
60	## Main declarations
61	
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelChartApp_eq` — the Abel chart's value at a point of the divisor
63	  scheme, as an explicit `Sigma.mk`.  Both components, since the datum needs both.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartLocusAffineLocal` — the `haff` residue, named.  This is what
65	  `chartLocusOpens` silently costs.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens_of_affineLocal` — `chartLocusOpens` from it, so the
67	  dependency is explicit in the API rather than in an argument position.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation` — the residue **reduced to B-4's
69	  own named obligation**: a per-affine-piece `IsChartDatumPresentation` gives it.  This is the
70	  link that was asserted in `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring and never written.
71	-/
72	
73	set_option autoImplicit false
74	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
75	
76	universe u
77	
78	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
79	
80	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
81	
82	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
83	
84	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
85	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
86	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
87	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
88	
89	noncomputable section
90	
91	/-! ## The Abel chart's value, both components -/
92	
93	/-- **The Abel chart map evaluated at a point of the divisor scheme.**
94	
95	`abelSigmaChart` is `rep.toSigmaExtension ≫ Over.sigmaExtensionNat (chartValueTrans …)`, and
96	both factors act componentwise on the Σ-extension, so the value at `x : Y ⟶ D.left` is the
97	pair whose structure morphism is `x ≫ D.hom` and whose class is the chart value of the divisor
98	family `rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)`.
99	
100	Recorded as an equation because a coverage producer has to match this against a *given*
101	section, and the match is two equations rather than one: the Σ-components must agree before
102	the classes are even in the same type.  Leaving it to unfold at the use site is how the
103	Σ-component gets forgotten. -/
104	@[simp]
105	theorem abelChartApp_eq {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
106	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
108	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
109	    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (x : Y ⟶ D.left) :
110	    (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app (op Y) x
111	      = ⟨x ≫ D.hom, ⟨chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x ≫ D.hom))
112	          (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)),
113	        chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg _ _⟩⟩ :=
114	  rfl
115	
116	/-! ## The `haff` residue, named
117	
118	`chartLocusOpens` takes the affine-local openness as an argument.  Naming it is not cosmetic:
119	an argument in a definition's signature is invisible to a census of open obligations, which is
120	how "the `W` field costs zero" survived into two roadmap rows. -/
121	
122	variable (C) in
123	/-- **The affine-local openness residue of `chartLocus`** — what `chartLocusOpens` costs.
124	
125	For a test `T` and a class `lam` on it, this says the chart locus is open over every affine
126	open piece of `T`.  It is exactly the `haff` argument of `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'`,
127	and it is the *only* remaining input to CHART-U(b) at a general test: the iso-invariance
128	hypothesis that used to sit beside it was discharged
129	(`isSplitWitnessIsoInvariant_holds`), but this one was passed through, not proved.
130	
131	Named as a `Prop` so that it appears in searches for open obligations. -/
132	def ChartLocusAffineLocal (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
133	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : Prop :=
134	  ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
135	    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))
136	
137	variable (C) in
138	/-- `chartLocusOpens` with its cost made explicit in the API.
139	
140	Identical in content to `chartLocusOpens` — the point is that the dependency is now a named
141	`Prop` a reader can grep for, rather than an unnamed argument that reads as bookkeeping. -/
142	def chartLocusOpens' (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
143	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
144	    (haff : ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam) : T.left.Opens :=
145	  chartLocusOpens C m Z T lam haff
146	
147	@[simp]
148	lemma mem_chartLocusOpens' {m : ℕ} {Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor}
149	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} {haff : ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam}
150	    {t : T.left} :
151	    t ∈ chartLocusOpens' C m Z T lam haff ↔ t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam :=
152	  Iff.rfl
153	
154	/-! ## Reducing the residue to B-4's own named obligation
155	
156	`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`'s docstring says the general-test statement follows from the
157	affine one "by the affine-piece locality of the (b-amendment)'s transport (iii)", and adds that
158	it "is not stated here only because it would need the presentation hypothesis *per affine
159	piece*".  That is right, and this is the statement it describes. -/
160	
161	set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in
162	variable (C π) in
163	/-- **The `haff` residue from a per-affine-piece presentation** — the link
164	`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring describes and does not state.
165	
166	For each affine open `U` of the test, a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `Γ(T.left, U)` presenting
167	the restricted twisted class gives openness of the locus on that piece
168	(`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation`), and `chartLocus` over the piece *is* that set
169	by definition (`chartLocus` unfolds to the split-witness set of the twisted class, and the
170	twist commutes with restriction by `picEtMap_chartTwist`).
171	
172	So the affine-local residue is **exactly** B-4's presentation obligation, quantified over
173	affine pieces — no extra geometry, and in particular nothing certificate- or divRep-gated.
174	Combined with `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` this closes CHART-U(b) at a general test the
175	moment `IsChartDatumPresentation` is available per piece.
176	
177	The `hπ` and `IsFinite π` hypotheses are the ones
178	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` carries.  `IsFinite π` is strictly stronger than
179	the file-level `IsAffineHom π` (whence the overlapping-instance warning, disabled below): the
180	affine openness route runs through the rigid engine, which needs finiteness, while the rest of
181	this file needs only affineness. -/
182	theorem chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation [IsFinite π]
183	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
184	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
185	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
186	    (hpres : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
187	      ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C (Γ(T.left, U.1)) π,
188	        IsChartDatumPresentation C π
189	          (chartTwist C m Z _ (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)) D) :
190	    ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam := by
191	  intro U
192	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := hpres U
193	  exact isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation C π hπ hD
194	
195	end
196	
197	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	
9	/-!
10	# DAT-B B-5: the coverage datum RE-SPELLED in the slice — and why that discharges nothing
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean:105` (`abelChartApp_eq`) records that the chart
13	application is a **pair**, and its header warns that a coverage producer must match *two*
14	equations rather than one — the Σ-components before the classes are even in the same type.
15	Two roadmap rows and the c9b thread price the coverage datum accordingly.
16	
17	**This file first claimed that price was avoidable.  It is not, and the retraction is the
18	content.**  The claim was: a producer working in the slice over `Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1)`, rather
19	than handing over a bare `x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ D.left`, gets the Σ-equation as `Over.w` "for
20	free".  What is true is that `Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ D` **is by definition** the pair of an
21	`x` and a proof that `x ≫ D.hom = W.ι ≫ s.1`: `(Over.homMk x hx).left = x` and
22	`Over.w (Over.homMk x hx) = hx` both hold by `rfl`, so the two hypotheses are interderivable
23	and a producer can do nothing here it could not do before.  Refuted by a fresh-context audit
24	(inbox `I-1021`); the durable lesson is `I-1024`.
25	
26	**The reusable error, since it is subtle.**  The non-vacuity check this file ran — `rfl` on
27	`x ≫ D.hom = W.ι ≫ s.1` at unconstrained `x` **fails** — was read as licensing the discount.
28	It forbids it.  An equation that is not definitionally free does not become free by moving
29	into a binder's type; it merely stops appearing as a goal, which is what made the report
30	convincing.  `slice_iff_bare` below is the one-line probe that settles such a question, and it
31	is landed so the claim cannot be re-made here.
32	
33	## What this file is, honestly
34	
35	A **re-spelling** of the coverage datum, with the pair equation traded for one class equation
36	plus a richer input type carrying the other.  `datum_of_slice` is one half of an equivalence
37	(`bare_of_slice` is the other), so by the `I-0896` criterion no obligation was reduced.  It is
38	worth keeping only because the slice spelling is the shape a divisor-side producer would want
39	— every such producer here is stated over `overSpec k S`, so a route through them needs the
40	identification of `Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1)` with `overSpec k Γ(Y, W)` at an affine `W`, and that
41	identification is against the slice form, not the bare one.  That seam is not written here.
42	
43	The class equation is untouched and is the whole of what remains: it asks that the chart value
44	of the divisor family named by `g` **is** the given class restricted.  Its cost is a divisor
45	family over a *neighbourhood* produced from data at a *point* — a spreading-out, measured
46	absent from the tree for this carrier by two independent censuses (every `DivFamZar` producer
47	takes its base ring or the affine-opens limit first; the only spreading lemmas,
48	`exists_supportTube` and its `Confine` instance, act on the support locus of an already-given
49	local-equation system, not on a class; mathlib's `spread_out_of_isGermInjective'` is about
50	morphism germs).
51	
52	**A second limit, and it is the sharper one.**  The two composites below are stated at the
53	**unrestricted** chart `abelSigmaChart`, whose source is all of `D.left`.
54	`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54` and `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14` both hold that antecedent 1 is
55	*false* there (the fibres are linear systems `|D|`, so it is not a monomorphism), while the
56	atlas the tree intends, `mixedParamChart`, has source `(V i : Scheme)`.  So these endpoints
57	supply antecedent 2 at a family where antecedent 1 fails, and the two do not co-instantiate —
58	`I-0861`'s V-coupling defect, filed here as `I-1022`.  The site content of
59	`Pic0ChartCoverageAffineTest.lean` is family-generic and does apply to `mixedParamChart`; only
60	these instantiated composites are stranded.

62	## Main declarations
63	
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.sigmaComponent_of_slice` — the Σ-component of a slice morphism, which is
65	  `Over.w`.  **Not a discharge**: see `slice_iff_bare`.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.slice_iff_bare` — **the refutation of this file's original claim**, in the
67	  kernel rather than in prose: a slice morphism over `Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1)` is exactly a bare
68	  morphism together with the Σ-equation, both directions by `rfl`.
69	* `AlgebraicGeometry.datum_of_slice` — the datum equation of `chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal`

94	
95	/-- **The Σ-component of a slice morphism is `Over.w`** — true, and *not* a discharge of the
96	coverage datum's Σ-equation.  Read it with `slice_iff_bare` immediately below, which is why. -/
97	theorem sigmaComponent_of_slice {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
98	    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (W : Y.Opens)
99	    (g : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ D) :
100	    g.left ≫ D.hom = W.ι ≫ s.1 :=
101	  Over.w g
102	
103	/-- **A slice morphism IS a bare morphism plus the Σ-equation** — the refutation of this
104	file's original "the Σ-component is absorbed for free" claim, stated so it cannot be re-made.
105	
106	Both directions are `rfl`: `Over.homMk` bundles `(x, hx)` into `g` with `g.left = x`, and
107	`Over.w` projects it back out.  So working in the slice **moves** the Σ-equation into the input
108	type; it does not discharge it, and a producer owes exactly what it owed before.  What changes
109	is only that the equation stops appearing as a goal — which is why the original claim looked
110	measured.

114	theorem slice_iff_bare {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
115	    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (W : Y.Opens) :
116	    Nonempty (Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ D) ↔
117	      ∃ x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ D.left, x ≫ D.hom = W.ι ≫ s.1 :=
118	  ⟨fun ⟨g⟩ => ⟨g.left, Over.w g⟩, fun ⟨x, hx⟩ => ⟨Over.homMk x hx⟩⟩
119

121

131	theorem datum_of_slice {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
132	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
133	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAffPullClause

/-!
# U2 as an equation between morphisms: the chart maps lie in the range of the classifier

`Picard/DivRepAffPullClause.lean` reduced the whole divisor-representability chain to a
single hypothesis, `DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause U`, and `IsChartClause.of_id` showed
that its `ω`-quantifier collapses to the identity point, i.e. to the DDR9-U ε-identity as
`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.1 states it.  That is still a *submodule* identity with
a `∀`-quantifier over tower tests and framings hidden inside `IsDivRepClassify`.

This file removes that quantifier.  The backward classifier `divRepClassifyZar`
(`Picard/DivRepClassifyZar.lean`) is defined for **every** locally certified class over
**every** affine test, unconditionally, and `isDivRepClassify_unique` says it is the
*only* morphism satisfying the clause.  So the clause is not an extra property at all:

> `IsDivRepClassify F₀ v` ↔ `(divRepClassifyZar … F₀).left = v`.

Both directions are one line — forward is uniqueness, backward is a rewrite — and the
consequence is that U2 becomes an **equation between two morphisms of schemes that both
already exist**:

> U2 ↔ for each pair chart `(i, j)`, `(divRepClassifyZar … (U i j)).left = ChartMap i j`.

Reading off the existential, the last obligation of divisor representability is that
each chart map lies in the **range** of the classifier at its own chart ring:

> `divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartRange` :
>   `(∀ i j, ∃ F, (divRepClassifyZar … F).left = ChartMap i j) →`
>   `(divFunctor C π g).RepresentableBy DivOver`

Since `divRepClassifyZar` is injective on classes (`eq_of_isDivRepClassify`,
`Picard/DivRepClassifyZarSep.lean`), representability of `divFunctor` is *equivalent* to
surjectivity of `divRepClassifyZar` at every affine test; what this file records is that
surjectivity at the **chart rings alone** suffices.  That is the honest content: the
classifier is already a bijection onto its range everywhere, and the whole remaining debt
is that the finitely many chart points are hit.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq` — the clause **is**
  the classifier equation, in both directions.  General: no chart family, no universal
  point.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepChartFamily.isChartClause_iff_forall_classify_eq` — U2 as a
  per-chart equation of morphisms, **as an iff**, so it is a reduction and not merely a
  restatement (the safeguard of inbox `I-0571`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartRange` — divisor
  representability from range membership of the chart maps.

## What this does NOT do

It produces no class over a chart ring, so it clears no gate: U2 is unproved and, per
roadmap `…divrep.u2`, the production of a chart class with the tautological ε remains the
G-4 obligation.  What changes is what a producer has to exhibit — a class whose classifier
*is* the chart map, rather than a family satisfying a quantified submodule identity.  The
endpoint also still carries `hO`, `hχ` and the ambient curve instances.
-/
